items.reason: FLT_LOG_LEN=16; length of flt_log circular buffer (used in flt_log[flt_idx++ & (FLT_LOG_LEN - 1)]).
k_trip_a=15.0f; overload trip threshold for i_rms (compared in prot_slow: if (i_rms > k_trip_a)).
ol_hold_ms=5000; overload ride-through time; prot_slow increments ol_ms and triggers inv_off/log_fault(FLT_OL) when ++ol_ms >= ol_hold_ms.

inline peak threshold 21.2f; prot_fast compares a=abs(i_pk) and trips immediately when (a > 21.2f) (inv_off(); log_fault(FLT_OC)). Intended as peak trip limit; exact mapping to iout_pk_limit depends on whether i_pk is true hardware-peak current vs RMS.
inline 0.9f multiplier in (vo_rms < 0.9f * VO_NOM); defines a low-voltage/brownout threshold band edge relative to VO_NOM (a factor, not an absolute voltage).
inline retry limit 3; prot_restart allows at most 3 retries (if (retry < 3) ... retry++).
inline delay_ms(500); restart backoff delay before inv_on during retry (delay_ms(500)).
FW_VER_MAJ at line 19 is a firmware major version identifier (explicitly labeled firmware id).
VIN_LO_XFER at line 22 is the AC input window lower transfer point: "go to battery below this, Vrms"; matches vin_min (lowest input voltage before transferring to battery).
VIN_HI_XFER at line 23 is the AC input window upper transfer point: "go to battery above this, Vrms"; matches vin_max (highest input voltage accepted before transferring to battery).
VBUS_REF at line 26 is the PFC regulation target ("PFC regulation target, V"); used as bus voltage setpoint, matching vbus_set concept.
VO_NOM at line 29 is nominal output voltage ("output, Vrms"); used as the output target, matching vout_set.
VO_TOL at line 30 is the ± regulation band tolerance relative fraction (0.03). It defines the band edges but is not itself a rule quantity.
VO_HI at line 31 is computed as VO_NOM * (1.0f + VO_TOL) (upper edge of output regulation band); matches vout_hi.
IO_RATED at line 32 is rated output current ("A rms, 1500 VA / 120 V"); matches iout_rated.
I_TRIP_RMS at line 33 is overload shutdown trip level ("overload shutdown, A rms"); matches iout_trip (software overload trip level).
TMR_LD at line 36 is PWM period register value ("PWM period, 25 kHz carrier"); matches pwm_period (period register counts).
DB_CNT at line 37 is dead-time count value ("dead time" / 300 us); matches pwm_deadband (dead-time register counts).
K_P at line 40 is the voltage-loop proportional gain ("voltage loop" and K_P). Matches vloop_kp.
K_I at line 41 is the voltage-loop integral gain per control ISR (commented). Matches vloop_ki.
VBAT_NOM at line 44 is battery string nominal voltage ("string nominal, V"); matches vbat_nom.
VBAT_CUT at line 45 is end of discharge / low-battery cutoff voltage ("end of discharge"); matches vbat_cutoff.
UART_BAUD at line 48 is UART/RS-232 port baud rate ("front-panel / RS-232 port"); matches comms_or_buffer category (UART baud). No specific rule id provided for baud.
PIN_BYP_RELAY at line 49 is a GPIO pin assignment for the static bypass relay drive; categorized as pin_map. No rule id applies.
ADC_FULL (line 9) is the ADC full-scale value used for scaling the ADC reading; it is 12-bit converter full-scale counts.
DAC_FULL (line 10) is the comparator reference DAC full-scale code (counts), used to derive the negative comparator DAC threshold.
VBUS_FS (line 13) is “V at ADC full scale” for the DC bus divider (1.5 M / 10 k), i.e., bus voltage at ADC full scale.
K_VS (line 14) is computed as (VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL) and represents volts per ADC count for the bus sense chain.
VBAT_FS (line 17) is “V at ADC full scale” for the battery divider (499 k / 10 k), i.e., battery voltage at ADC full scale.

VO_FS_PK (line 20) is “peak V at +/- half scale” for the output voltage sense (mid-rail biased). This matches the concept of vout_fs_pk (peak at the edge of the mid-rail-biased sense range), though the exact ADC-to-peak mapping isn’t further shown in the snippet.

IO_FS_PK (line 23) is “peak A at +/- half scale” for the output current sense (mid-rail biased). This matches the concept of iout_fs_pk (peak at the edge of the mid-rail-biased current-sense range), inferred from the comment and name.
CMP_DAC_HI (line 24) is the positive overcurrent comparator trip code; it directly corresponds to the hardware peak-current limit DAC code for the positive direction (iout_pklim_dac_hi).
CMP_DAC_LO (line 25) is computed as (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI), forming the negative comparator DAC code; corresponds to iout_pklim_dac_lo.
